nodes.natural_language: Given condition on x and y
Rewrite objective expression by completing the square

nodes.statement: |x+y| + |x-y| = 2 max(|x|,|y|) so hypothesis equivalent to max(|x|,|y|)=1

nodes.natural_language: Objective rewrites as (x-3)^2 + y^2 - 9, so maximize (x-3)^2 + y^2 on max(|x|,|y|)=1
nodes.statement: x^2 - 6x + y^2 = (x-3)^2 + y^2 - 9 and max(|x|,|y|)=1 imply maximize (x-3)^2 + y^2 subject to max(|x|,|y|)=1

nodes.natural_language: Feasible set is boundary of square, objective maximized at vertices
nodes.statement: The feasible set is thus the boundary of the square [-1,1]×[-1,1], and (x-3)^2+y^2 is maximized at the vertices (-1,±1)

nodes.natural_language: Bound the variables from the max condition
Bound (x-3)^2 + y^2 on the square boundary
nodes.statement: (x-3)^2 + y^2 is at most 16 + 1 = 17 (attained at x = -1, |y| = 1)
At (-1, \pm 1) we obtain (x-3)^2 + y^2 = 17, so the objective equals 8

nodes.natural_language: Check value at remaining vertices to confirm maximizer
nodes.statement: The remaining vertices (1,±1) give the strictly smaller value 5-9=-4.

nodes.natural_language: Verify that the candidate vertices satisfy the constraint
nodes.statement: The vertices (-1,±1) lie on the feasible set since |(-1)+1|+|(-1)-1|=2 (and likewise for the other sign)

nodes.natural_language: Conclude the maximum value from verified maximizer
nodes.statement: Hence the maximum of the original expression is 8

nodes.natural_language: Maximum value of expression is 8, hence answer D
nodes.statement: max(x^2-6x+y^2)=8 under the given constraint, so the answer is 8
At (-1,1) we have max(|x|,|y|)=1 so the constraint holds, and (x-3)^2+y^2=17 hence the original expression equals 8.

nodes.natural_language: Equality in the bound (x-3)^2+y^2\le17 is attained inside the feasible set
nodes.statement: Equality in the bound (x-3)^2+y^2\le17 is attained inside the feasible set, so the maximum of the original expression is exactly 8
